note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address, price, opening time and lighting statement comes from the City of Scottsdale's own pages: its pickleball page for the counts, addresses and hours, and each park's own page for the cost and the sharing rules. The City lists five locations; four are published here, and the one that is not is named below with the reason. Ashler Hills Park joined this page on 4 September 2026, when this site added a second address resolver; see the last question below.

slots.parking: Scottsdale publishes nothing about parking at any of the four venues. All four are suburban parks in the north and east of the city rather than street-grid sites, and Ashler Hills is the furthest out, near Cave Creek. That is a reading of the map, not a fact from the City.
slots.peak_hours:
This is the first city page in the directory where this section is written from a source rather than from inference. Scottsdale states it, in the same words, on three of the four park pages: "Mornings are typically the busiest time for pickleball play" at Cholla, at Horizon and at Thompson Peak.

The City pairs it with a sharing rule. Play is standard format, first to 11 and win by two, with a 30-minute time limit, "at which time players should rotate off the court with any waiting players". So a queue at 9 a.m. is a queue that moves. Nothing is reservable in Scottsdale: courts are first come, first served, and no amplified sound is permitted. Ashler Hills' park page names "8 lighted pickleball courts" and says nothing else, so neither the rotation rule nor the peak-time note is stated for that park.
slots.surface_condition: No surface is stated for any Scottsdale court, which is ordinary: few cities in this directory have ever published one. What the City does publish is maintenance history: Thompson Peak Park's three courts were closed from 17 August to 11 September 2026 for resurfacing, and were expected to reopen on the 12th, weather permitting. That is why Thompson Peak is published as closed.
slots.local_scene: Twenty-nine verified courts across four parks, every one of them lit, and three of the four free to use in the City's own words. Horizon Park's ten courts are the largest single count; Cholla and Ashler Hills have eight each and Thompson Peak has three. The City also runs a free public drop-in programme on Scottsdale Community College's six lighted courts. That venue is not published here because the Census places 9000 E Chaparral Rd outside the city limits, but it is real and it is free.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts
best_for.text: Horizon Park has ten lighted courts, the largest count in Scottsdale and one of the larger sets anywhere in this directory. Free, drop-in, not reservable, open from sunrise to 10:30 p.m. daily. The City says mornings are typically busiest here, and the sharing rule that applies (30-minute games, rotate off for anyone waiting) is what makes ten courts feel like ten rather than like four occupied ones.

best_for.heading: Best if you are playing in the evening
best_for.text: Any of them: all four published Scottsdale venues are lit and all four run to 10:30 p.m. Cholla Park is the pick if you want eight courts without Horizon's crowd. The City marks it "Eight outdoor lighted courts", free to use, drop-in and not reservable. In a city where summer daytime play is barely an option, sunrise-to-10:30 p.m. lighting at every venue is the single most valuable thing Scottsdale publishes.

best_for.heading: Best if you do not want to pay
best_for.text: Three of the four state it outright: "They are free to use" appears on the park pages for Cholla, Horizon and Thompson Peak. Across this whole directory only six other cities have a verified free court, and only because their operators wrote the word down too. Ashler Hills is not a paid venue as far as anyone knows; its park page lists the courts among the park’s features and says nothing about cost, so its price is unstated rather than confirmed.

best_for.heading: Best if you are in far north Scottsdale
best_for.text: Ashler Hills Park has eight lighted courts at the northern edge of the city, open sunrise to 10:30 p.m. like every Scottsdale venue. It is the least documented of the four: its park page lists "8 lighted pickleball courts" among the park’s features and stops there, so the price and the rotation rule the City publishes elsewhere are not stated for it. It is also the newest addition to this page, having been unpublishable until this site added a second address resolver in September 2026.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Scottsdale have?
faqs.a: Twenty-nine across four City of Scottsdale venues: ten at Horizon Park, eight each at Cholla Park and Ashler Hills Park, and three at Thompson Peak Park. All are outdoor and lit, and none can be booked.

Mornings, at the three venues where the City says so: "Mornings are typically the busiest time for pickleball play" appears on the Cholla, Horizon and Thompson Peak pages. This is the only city in this directory whose operator has published a peak time, so it is the only city page here where that answer is a fact rather than an inference.
At three of the four, yes: each of those park pages states "They are free to use". Ashler Hills reads "not verified yet" on cost because its page names the courts and never mentions what they cost.

faqs.q: Why is Thompson Peak Park shown as closed?
faqs.a: Because the City says it is. All three courts were closed from Monday 17 August to Friday 11 September 2026 for resurfacing, and are expected to reopen on Saturday 12 September, weather permitting. This page was checked on 4 September, inside that window.

faqs.q: Why did Ashler Hills Park only appear recently?
faqs.a: Because its address could not be resolved until 4 September 2026. A venue must have a street address that resolves before it is published, and the US Census address file has no record of 32220 N. 74th Way. That day a second resolver, OpenStreetMap, was added. It resolves this address, so the courts now publish.

Three of the four published addresses were matched by the Census address geocoder and placed in the incorporated place "Scottsdale city", Maricopa County, AZ. 9000 E Chaparral Rd matched but returned no incorporated place at all, which is why Scottsdale Community College is not published. 32220 N. 74th Way returned no match, which is why Ashler Hills Park needed a second resolver. The second address resolver this site added on 4 September 2026, consulted only where the Census address file has no record and accepted only at house-number level. It resolves 32220 N. 74th Way to "32220, North 74th Way, Scottsdale, Maricopa County, Arizona", which is what allows Ashler Hills Park and its eight lighted courts to be published.
